info.title: Your RQTH orientation, before entering the working world
info.lead: HandiDiag is for students of the school preparing to work: it helps you see whether official recognition (RQTH) could make sense for your career plan, and who to talk to.
info.what: The RQTH (recognition of the status of disabled worker, in France) is an administrative decision. It can give access to measures for finding or keeping a job, such as workplace or schedule adjustments and financial support. It concerns people whose ability to get or keep a job is reduced by a lasting impairment of physical, sensory, mental or psychological functions. The application is personal and voluntary.
info.what_falc: The RQTH is a decision made by the French administration. It can help you find a job or keep it. For example: adapted hours, an adapted workstation, money for equipment. The application is personal. Nobody can make it for you.
does: It explains the process in plain words.
It first asks whether the school's disability office follows you, then asks about twelve questions with no medical detail (about 6 minutes).
It tells you whether it may be useful to talk to someone, and who.
It gives you a kit to move forward: official links, checklist, steps.
does_falc: It explains the process in simple words.
It first asks if the disability office follows you. Then it asks about 12 questions. None is medical.
It says if it may help to talk to someone, and who.
It gives official links and a to-do list.
not: It never says whether you will be granted recognition: only the MDPH decides.
It does not replace a doctor, the MDPH or an adviser.
It sends your answers to nobody.
not_falc: It does not make a diagnosis.
It does not say if you will get the RQTH. The MDPH decides.
It does not replace a doctor or an adviser.
It sends your answers to nobody.
privacy: No account, no email address requested.
Your answers stay in your browser. They disappear when you reload or close the page.
Only anonymous counters (for example: number of completed questionnaires) may be sent. You can refuse below.
No cookie, no tracker, no third-party service.
privacy_falc: Your answers stay on your device. They are erased when you close the page.
We only count how many people finished. We do not know who. You can say no below.

flags.urgent: You have a deadline coming up. Processing times for an application can be long: if you want to act, it is better to ask for advice now.
flags.needs_info: You know little about the RQTH. The resource kit explains the process step by step.
flags.stigma: Fear of other people's judgement is common. The process is personal and voluntary. A trusted contact can explain what is shared, with whom, and what stays confidential.
flags.employer: Applying for the RQTH is a personal step: you do not have to tell your employer or school in order to find out more or to apply.
flags.complexity: The file can seem heavy. The kit offers a checklist and simple steps, and the MDPH or an adviser can help you fill it in.
flags.who: You don't know who to turn to: the list below offers starting points suited to your situation.
flags.time: Lack of time is a common obstacle. A first conversation can happen in a single appointment or call.
flags.informal_adjust: You have adjustments with no official framework. Recognition can help secure them over time: a contact person can tell you whether it suits your case.
flags.no_support: You are not yet supported. A first contact with one of the contacts below is a good starting point.
flags.already_rqth: Remember to check the end date of your recognition and plan its renewal with the MDPH.
flags.see_doctor: A doctor fills in the medical certificate for the application. If you have no follow-up, a general practitioner, the student health service or the occupational physician can be a first contact.
flags.student_exam: For exams: your institution's disability office can explain which adjustments exist and how far ahead to ask. Plan before the exam period.
flags.student_work: For an internship or work-study: the host company may have a disability officer. You choose what you share, and when.
flags.shift_work: Your hours are irregular: the occupational physician can recommend adjustments to hours or pace.
flags.long_search: Your job search has lasted a long time: France Travail and Cap emploi offer specialised support.
flags.public_status: Rules may differ depending on your status. The disability officer or prevention physician can tell you what applies.
flags.for_relative: The process is personal: only the person concerned can apply. You can help, without deciding for them.
flags.for_support: You are looking into this to support someone: respect their confidentiality and their choice to share, or not.
flags.psych_support_none: You have no identified support: a health professional, the student health service or the occupational physician can be a first contact. If you are in distress, do not stay alone: in France, 3114 is available 24/7.
flags.life_sleep: If your sleep is disturbed, this is something to raise with a doctor.
flags.emp_unaware: Your manager is not aware: you do not have to tell them in order to find out more. The occupational physician is bound by medical confidentiality.
flags.emp_leave: Sick leave linked to these difficulties: talking to the occupational physician may allow adjustments to be considered to reduce it.
flags.sup_confidentiality: Do not share anything about a person's health without their agreement.
flags.goal_info_only: You only want to get information: the resource kit is enough to start; nothing obliges you to go further.

kit.title: Resource kit
kit.intro: Everything you need to move forward, with official sources. Always check forms and the list of documents on the official websites: they can change.
kit.checklist_intro: Tick items as you go. Nothing is saved: if you reload the page, the list is emptied.
checklist: Read the official page about the RQTH
Find the MDPH for my département
Note my difficulties and their effects on my studies or work
Book an appointment with a doctor for the medical certificate
Fill in the application form, including the “life project” section
Gather the requested documents (official list): ID, proof of address, useful medical documents
Submit the file (online or by post) and keep a copy
Note the submission date and watch for the reply letter

guide.title: Find out more
guide.text: Read the official page and the summary on this page. You do not have to decide anything at this stage.

guide.title: Talk to someone you trust
guide.text: A disability officer, an occupational or prevention physician, an adviser: your orientation list suggests starting points.

guide.title: See a doctor
guide.text: A doctor fills in a medical certificate describing the effects of your health situation. You can bring it with your file.

guide.title: Prepare the file
guide.text: Fill in the MDPH application form and gather the requested documents. Do not hesitate to ask the MDPH or an adviser for help.

guide.title: Submit the application
guide.text: The application goes to the MDPH of your département, online or by post. Keep a copy of everything you send.

guide.title: Wait for the decision
guide.text: The CDAPH commission decides. Waiting times vary by area (département). Once you receive the decision, you choose who you tell.

vigilance: HandiDiag does not replace a doctor, the MDPH or an adviser.
Always check forms and the list of documents on the official websites.
Keep the original of your decision notice.
Do not share medical information through insecure channels.

todo.posture: Workstations and postures: a conversation with the occupational physician, the prevention physician or the disability office can help look at a suitable chair, sit-stand alternation or adapted equipment.
todo.conc_energy: Tiredness affects concentration: planned breaks or an adapted pace can be raised with your contact person.
todo.commute: Commuting is tiring: partial remote work, staggered hours or transport support are leads to raise.
todo.breaks: You need breaks: you can ask for them to be planned (in class, in exams or during the working day).
todo.schedule_time: Your difficulties depend on the time of day: adapted hours can be discussed.
todo.reading_writing: Reading, writing or calculating take longer: extra time, adapted-format documents, text-to-speech or an adapted typeface are often-mentioned adjustments.
todo.organisation: Memory and organisation: planning tools, written instructions and regular check-ins can be discussed.
todo.listening: Following meetings or classes orally is hard: written materials, minutes and, with consent, recording can help.
todo.try_tools: While waiting for a conversation, free tools (text-to-speech, reminders, lists) can be tried.
todo.vision: Vision: magnification, contrast, screen readers and adapted documents can be requested.
todo.hearing: Hearing: captioning, hearing loops and written materials can be discussed.
todo.lighting: Lighting and seating: worth mentioning to the disability officer or the occupational physician.
todo.access: Access to premises: lifts, parking spaces or accessible rooms can be requested.
todo.equipment: Gestures and handling: ergonomic equipment or dictation software can be raised.
todo.oral_groups: Group or oral situations: advance preparation, an alternative format or a small group can be discussed.
todo.pace: Pressure and overload: spreading out deadlines or prioritising with a manager can be discussed.
todo.environment: Noise or the unexpected: a quiet space or changes announced in advance can help.
todo.diary: Your difficulties vary: keeping a simple diary (difficult days, what helps) makes it easier to talk to a professional and to put a file together.
todo.life_wide: Beyond work or studies, daily life is affected: you can mention it to a professional, other forms of support may exist.
todo.exam_request: Exam adjustments: ask early, well before the exam period, through the disability office (extra time, separate room, computer, breaks…).
todo.disclosure: Whether to tell the company is your choice: a conversation with the disability office or a doctor can help you decide what to share, and when.
todo.work_adapt: Internship or work-study: hours, commuting or workstation can be adjusted; ask the disability office and the company's disability officer.
todo.contact_school: Contact the disability office or administration: a first appointment does not commit you to any official process.
todo.transition: At the end of your studies, planning the move into work (adjustments, contacts) can avoid a break in rights; recognition obtained during studies helps.
todo.manager_ok: Your manager is aware: a short written note on the agreed adjustments, even a simple one, helps make them last.
todo.workstation_study: Workstation (chair, screen, noise): you can ask the occupational physician for a workstation assessment.
todo.org_work: Work organisation (hours, travel, pace): worth raising with the occupational physician and HR.
todo.occ_visit: You can ask for a visit with the workplace prevention and health service, on your own initiative.
todo.interview: Interviews and tests: adjustments (format, duration, video call) can be requested when applying; Cap emploi or your adviser can help.
todo.js_org: Commuting and long days: favour remote work or adapted hours in your search, and tell employers if you wish.
todo.training: Training: training and support schemes exist; Cap emploi, France Travail and Agefiph can inform you.
todo.js_contact: Contact your France Travail adviser to be directed to specialised support (Cap emploi).
todo.prevention_doc: Make an appointment with the prevention physician: they are bound by medical confidentiality.
todo.referent: Ask who the disability officer in your administration is (HR department, intranet).
todo.posting: A change of post or department is planned: it is a good time to ask for adjustments suited to the new post.
todo.keep_job: An early conversation with a contact person helps see which adjustments are possible before difficulties get worse.
todo.funding: Financial support: Agefiph (private sector) and FIPHFP (public sector) present the available aid; the MDPH processes applications.
todo.secure: Securing things over time: official recognition can formalise adjustments; a professional will tell you whether it suits your case.
todo.written: You prefer writing: you can ask for an appointment by email and for a written summary.
todo.remote_contact: You can ask for a remote appointment (phone or video call).
todo.small_steps: Little time available: move forward in small steps, for example one checklist step a week.
todo.helper: Getting help: a social worker, the disability office or an association can help put the file together.
todo.how_to_talk: To talk about it with the person: listen without judging, offer without imposing, respect their pace and confidentiality.
todo.sup_resources: You can share the resource kit's official links and point the person to a trusted contact.
todo.sup_setup: Putting adjustments in place goes through the disability officer or the occupational physician; the person chooses what they share.
todo.sup_aware: Raising awareness: Agefiph (private sector) and FIPHFP (public sector) offer resources and training.
todo.sup_legal: Legal questions: the disability officer, HR, Cap emploi or the MDPH can answer.
todo.prev_ready: Finding out in advance is a good idea: the resource kit will be useful if your situation changes.
todo.prev_share: You can share the HandiDiag link with someone who might need it.
todo.watch: A change ahead: spot signals early (lasting tiredness, difficulties settling in) and talk to a contact person before it weighs on you.
todo.pole_member_rqth: You are followed by the disability office: at your next meeting you can ask whether an RQTH fits your career plan and get help preparing the file.
todo.pole_join_yes: You would like to join the disability office: a simple e-mail to Charlie Dupic or Stéphanie Libeskind is enough for a first conversation (details below).
todo.rqth_work_value: In the working world, an RQTH can give access to workstation or schedule adjustments, financial aid (Agefiph) and specialised support. It commits you to nothing: you choose who to tell, and when.
todo.alternance_rqth: Work-study: depending on the case, an RQTH can open aid for you and for the company. Ask the disability office and Agefiph before signing.
todo.rqth_delay: Processing an RQTH file can take several months: if an internship, work-study or contract is coming up, it is better to start early.
todo.recruit_adapt: Online tests or interviews: you can ask for an adjustment (extra time, adapted format, breaks). You choose what you explain, and when.

admin.hint_login: Credentials are set when the server starts (see the README). In demo mode they are shown in the server console.
admin.base_hidden: Basis of this chart: {u}, but fewer than {n} (too few to show percentages)
admin.daily_b: completed, counted over the period (days with fewer than {k} are hidden and not counted)
admin.demo_text: To present the dashboard without waiting for real users, you can add FAKE journeys (spread over 10 days), then reset everything before real use.
admin.demo_confirm: Reset ALL counters to zero? This cannot be undone.
admin.verify_title: How to check that it works (2 minutes)
admin.v1: Open the site in another tab (`http://localhost:3000`) and start the questionnaire without finishing it: here, “Started journeys” goes up by 1.
admin.v2: Finish it up to the result: “Completed journeys” goes up by 1, and the orientation level obtained gains 1 in the charts.
admin.v3: Click an official link in the kit or “Download as PDF”: “Pages and documents viewed” gains 1.
admin.v4: Come back here: click “Refresh” (or wait 15 seconds, updates are automatic). “Last event received” shows “a few seconds ago”.
admin.v5: Only seeing “fewer than {k}”? That is normal: the privacy threshold hides small numbers. To test locally, restart the server with `$env:MIN_COUNT="1"; node server.js` (PowerShell), or add fake data with `node tools/seed-demo.js`.
admin.gl3d: Completed journeys ÷ started journeys. A low rate can mean a questionnaire that is too long, or people giving up.
admin.gl4d: The level proposed at the end: learn more, useful conversation, quick conversation advised, or already recognised. It is never a diagnosis.
admin.gl5d: The number of cases counted in the chart. The smaller n is, the less representative the chart.
admin.gl6d: Hidden value: too few people to publish without risk of recognising someone.
admin.dash_lead: What the tool does, without ever knowing who uses it.
admin.demo_notice: These figures contain FAKE demo data. Reset the counters (“Demo tools” at the bottom of the page) before real use.
admin.default_pw: You are using the demo password. Change it (“Change password” at the bottom of the page) before going online.
admin.masked: Some values are hidden (“fewer than {k}”): the privacy threshold protects small numbers. See “How to check that it works” to test.
admin.k3n: Not enough data (fewer than {k} started journeys)
admin.k4c: {r} % of started journeys chose to go further
admin.c1e: Breakdown of the results shown. “Quick conversation advised” flags important or repeated effects reported; it is not a diagnosis.
admin.c2e: Who the tool serves: useful to adapt the content. This edition is for the school's students.
admin.c3e: Interface language when the journey started.
admin.c4e: Official links opened and files generated (print, PDF, summary). Shows which resources really help.
admin.pw_mismatch: The confirmation does not match the new password.
admin.pw_ok: Password changed. Other sessions have been closed.
admin.pw_too_short: The new password is too short (10 characters minimum).
admin.pw_too_weak: This password is too weak or already known.
admin.pw_too_many_attempts: Too many attempts, try again later.
